beats: Hook: four program qubits must all talk to each other; the chip has four qubits wired in a ring (p20): a square table with a tall centrepiece, where each guest can talk only to the two guests on the neighbouring sides (line_qc_square_table). Find a seating plan, or prove there is none. Cast as in QC02-02: the head waiter (compiler), the guests (program qubits), the chairs (physical qubits).
The coupling graph comes from the resonators (p19, 59:24-59:54; the chip micrograph is covered): recall QC02-01's line_qc_string_village.

Qubit mapping = deciding who sits where (line_qc_place_cards); like register allocation, with limited connections in place of limited registers (61:22-62:16, clip): a desk with room for three folders, the rest in the cabinet (line_qc_desk_few_folders; reuse line_card_catalog).

The program is fully connected, a CNOT between every pair (reuse line_cp_handshake_party); the chip is a ring, so every seating leaves two pairs across the flowers: no perfect initial mapping (p21, 62:26-64:14, clip 63:49-64:14) (line_qc_crumpled_plans).
SWAP (p22, 64:35-65:51): two neighbours trade chairs mid-dinner and the blocked pairs become neighbours (line_qc_swap_seats); the mapping changes as the program runs.

The bill (66:18-67:45, clip 66:18-67:16): each SWAP is three CNOTs; with an illustrative budget of about 200 gates, a 150-gate program plus 20 SWAPs (60 CNOTs) is 210 and breaks it (line_qc_plate_tower; say it is illustrative). Worked example from the 2024 deck, Q24-01 p38: 6 -> 9 gates, depth 5 -> 8 after one SWAP (taped).
Fewest SWAPs is NP-complete (e.g. Siraichi et al. 2018; FACTS.md first): the seatings to try grow very fast (reuse line_heap). Next part: how her group's SABRE searches.
Cover (line_qc_cover_qc02_04; for the X post and thumbnails, not a film beat): the head waiter has two neighbours at the square table trade chairs.

drawings.name: line_qc_square_table
drawings.prompt: Seen from slightly above and in front: a square dinner table with one chair on each side and, in the middle of the table, a very tall, bushy flower arrangement in a vase that blocks the view straight across the table. The four guests, one on each side: a tall guest with a high top-knot bun and a long striped scarf on the left side, a short, round guest with a flat cap and a cardigan with big round buttons on the near side with the back to us, a guest with long straight hair held back by a headband and a plain dress with a wide round collar on the far side facing us, a guest with curly hair and a thick roll-neck jumper on the right side. The guests on neighbouring sides chat happily across the corners, but the left guest and the right guest each lean far sideways, craning to see round the flowers at each other, without success. All the guests are invented characters with simple round faces and dot eyes. Square image 1024x1024; the table and the four guests fill about 88% of the width and about 85% of the height. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos.
